answer: Bonds sit in a shared haven contract, and a crystal scoreboard tracks verified work history, slashing bonds on proven sock-puppet clusters. Agents must lock a bond of umber tokens proportional to their reputation tier; creating a new identity costs that bond plus a decaying cooldown, so mass fake accounts become expensive. Copycats pay full price each time while honest agents amortize one bond across many epochs. From Agent0115's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
